items.mnemonic: Twenty jobs on the list, a hungry mouth at home, a king who expects results, and still you find the power to arrive before dawn: that is diligence.
On the road a corpse-still figure waits while a sheep ambles across at its own pace; everything today will be late.
A corpse-quiet figure sits under the eaves with ten chairs around and one mouth humming an old tune; someone still chooses to reside here.
Nine twigs from a tree and one small bird's abandoned nest, all tossed into the same drawer: a miscellaneous jumble.
A hand waves from the doorway, the sword is set down by the step, and a mouth calls out a warm welcome: invite.
A yawn so wide the whole face stretches open, and you can see that something is missing inside: a lack.
One sun sinks to where its path makes a cross on the horizon, and the whole day resets to renew itself.
A boar's tusk mark on the gatepost, deepened with a sword every year, is how the family chose to engrave the passing hours.
Husband beside husband, each holding up a shell coin, nodding together at the plan: we approve.
A hand reaches out to wrap around a sleepy snake and draw it close against the chest: a gentle embrace.
A dog has chewed straight through the wax seal on the storehouse door; breaking that seal is a crime.
The craft workshop falls silent as a black sail glides past the window, and every heart inside clenches with fear.
Air slides in through the nose, sinks to the heart, and drifts back out: one slow breath.
Push open the door and a big dog is waiting with your slippers; of course you return.
On the cliff edge stands a white shrine; a small figure bows the head and whispers a wish.
Run at the wall with a halberd for a vaulting pole, plant it, and cross over in one leap.
Deep in the valley a mouth opens in a yawn so hungry it echoes off both slopes: pure desire.
Under the sickness roof a beak pecks the one foot you still utilize for walking, and every step is pain.
Two hooks lock into each other so that neither can let go first: a grip that is mutual.
Stalks gathered and tied tight around the middle make a sheaf, which is simply a bundle.
A person stands beside a mirror, whereby everyone can see how closely the two faces resemble each other.
A bone laid beside a sword, then another pair, then another, all set out in one straight row.
A hand dips into a hole at the foot of the tree, feeling blindly for the dropped key: a careful search.
A bad omen flashes across the sky and everyone takes to the road at a sprint: escape.
It takes real talent to swing the heavy gate shut with one arm, but you manage to close it.
A thread wound by an old woman since the first sun of the year grows into one long cord that ties everything together.
A hand brings an axe down on a green branch; it does not split, it only creases into a fold.
Grass, a sinking sun, one big field, and another sun tomorrow: day after day is how we live.
Something has gone wrong and the heart beneath it sinks: sad.
A hand lifts the sign over a mound of earth, then more earth, and props it on a divination stick for a hook: hang it there.
The runner is about to arrive when a sword flashes at the finish line to cut the ribbon; now you truly arrive.
Ice chips tinkle as a guest fakes a long yawn, slides a hand over the silver dish, and tucks it under his coat: steal.
The mouth opens and the lungs reach out for the cool morning air, pulling it all the way in: inhale.
On the hill the sun climbs over one flag snapping in the breeze and floods the slope with sunshine.
Step forward at noon, stop at the gate, and show the seal: that is how you approach the honorable lord.
The mouth stretches wide as if in a yawn, then pushes the air out hard enough to kill the candle: blow.
A young woman with one drop of her mother's stubborn streak in her: the daughter.
You say it with a confident mouth, but one plus one does not make eight: a mistake.
The heart of a mother counts the same shell coins every morning until her fingers are accustomed to the motion.
Eight cuts of the sword divide a single shell coin among the whole family, and each piece is tiny: poor.
A woman raises her right hand to point at the broken vase, and the heart below pounds with anger.
On the family altar sits a shelf of faded portraits; every face is an ancestor.
Under the sickness roof even the skin sags, and the whole body admits it is tired.
A fire on the west side of the field sends grey ribbons curling up from the earth: smoke.
The heart leaps when an arm reaches out from behind the cloth curtain: scary.
A single nail driven into the head of the mountain marks its summit.
Long streaks fall past the arm as the right hand combs them smooth: hair.
A sprout bursting up through a plank in one bold stroke: raw talent.
Leather stretched by a person over a spoon-shaped wooden last: a shoe.
The ear turns red long before the heart admits it: shame.
A person turns the corner and bumps into a monkey wearing the very same hat, purely accidentally.
One person stands calm on the stockade wall while everyone else runs about in a panic: great.
Cocoon after cocoon hangs above a person who counts them with a halberd for a pointer: how many?
Two slim stalks with leaves drooping from the top joint: bamboo.
One tree beside another tree, close enough for the branches to touch: woods.
A tree, a tree, and a tree stacked into a crown: enough to call it a forest.
Water curled up in the garden like a scorpion's tail: a pond.
A mountain made of one giant stone: a rock.
Two slopes open like a mouth with a deep crease between them: a valley.
Two wings side by side, every barb drawn as a little tick: feathers.
A single curling strand with a hook at the bottom: fur.
A hand peels one long strip off the frame: skin.
Tall stalks with a trailing root drawn underneath: wheat.
Water that clings to the stem of the plant and refuses to run off is not water at all; it is oil.
From the earth a person scrapes white grains, tests one with the mouth, and pours the rest into a dish: salt.
A king's three bars with one extra drop glinting at the hip: a jewel.
A fat body, a stinger tail, and one dot of an eye: insect.
Something born of the sun and hung in the night sky: a star.
Rain gathers above and a curl of cloud swirls below, all of it one great cloud.
One tree and an inch of road measured out beside it: the start of a village.
A bird comes to rest on a mountain top rising out of the sea: an island.
An eye dangles from a fishhook over a small map, watching over the whole prefecture.
A box with a cross marked inside it on the city map: this ward.
Walking legs stop at every door and a mouth says the same greeting to each.
A wide shallow bowl standing on a foot ring: a dish.
A lidded pot on a tall stand, the kind that keeps one small thing: a bean.
A gold disc polished until it rings with a clear sound when tapped, propped up on two legs: a mirror.
A tree cut and joined into a small table you can write at: a desk.
From the tree ten shoots grow, and a right hand snaps one off: a branch.
A tree cut down to a vermilion-stained stump; the roots left in the ground are the stock.
Water with one frozen drop clinging to its side becomes a single ice block: ice.
Water drips from the clothesline in the summer sun, just like the sweat on your neck.
Water so wide that ten villages, each a thirsty mouth, see the same moon floating on it at night: a lake.
Water left under the sun beside one flag until it steams: hot water.
A small fire hung on a nail beside the door: a lamp.
An arm rakes through what is left of last night's fire: ash.
Up the mountain, under the cliff, a slow fire blackens the wood into charcoal.
